newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt court begins trial of teenaged militant.
newsitem.headline: Egypt court begins trial of teenaged militant.

text.p: A suspected Moslem militant went on trial in an Egyptian State Security court on Tuesday charged with killing five policemen and two civilians when he was 14 years old, court sources said.

They said Mohammed Ali el-Badri, 18, was supposed to be tried as a juvenile according to a new law that allows the trial and imprisonment of suspected militants who committed crimes while less than 18 but the judge decided Badri should face the charges as an adult.

Judge Ismail Hamdi did not give a reason for his decision which means that Badri now faces the death sentence if convicted. As a juvenile, Badri would have faced a sentence ranging from three to 25 years in prison with hard labour.
Hamdi also decided the charges against Badri should be combined with another set he faces in a case known as the "Great Assassinations" case.

In that case, Badri is being tried in a State Security court, along with 32 other suspected militants, on charges of trying to overthrow the government, killing 26 policemen and carrying out several other violent attacks.
He is being tried as an adult in that case although he was less than 18 years old when he allegedly took part in the crimes.
A lawyer for the defence in the "Great Assassinations" case told the court on Tuesday that the prosecution could not prove that his clients, including Badri, committed the alleged crimes.
The case was adjourned until Wednesday.
Moslem militants launched a bloody campaign in 1992 to overthrow the government and set up a strict Islamic state.
More than 1,000 people, mainly militants and policemen, have been killed in political violence since then.
